entries.title: What's New & in-app Feedback
entries.summary: This release adds a running changelog that greets you after every upgrade, plus a one-click way to send feedback straight to the team as a GitHub issue — optionally with a screenshot of what you're looking at.
highlights: A “What's new?” dialog now appears automatically the first time you open the app after an update.
A Feedback button sits next to Settings so you can report a bug or share an idea without leaving the app.
Attach a screenshot of your current screen and AI turns your note into a well-structured GitHub issue.

details.heading: What's New dialog
items: Summarizes every change between your previous version and the one you just installed.
Expand any release to read the full detail list, grouped by area.
Reopen it any time from Settings → About → “What's new”.

details.heading: Feedback
items: Pick a topic (General, Bugs, or Requests and ideas) and describe what happened.
Optionally capture a screenshot of your current screen for visual issues.
AI drafts a clear title and reproducible issue body, then files it in the project's GitHub repo and links you to it.

entries.title: Newsletter studio & Code Flow reliability
entries.summary: A big polish pass on the Newsletter experience and a batch of Code Flow PR-card fixes so pushes, updates, and review agents behave the way you'd expect.
highlights: Newsletter is now a full studio with appearance controls, chat image uploads, and faithful email rendering.
Code Flow PR cards show every reviewer and keep their Git section in sync with the review worktree.
Review agents now self-heal instead of showing “Ready” for an agent the CLI can't find.

details.heading: Newsletter
items: Redesigned into a studio layout with background, accent, font, size, and width controls.
Drag, drop, or paste images into chat and the assistant embeds and reflows them.
Emails now match the preview exactly, with charts and hero images rasterized so they survive mail clients.
Removed the redundant header Generate button; the assistant recovers context on its own when revising.

details.heading: Code Flow
items: PR cards list all reviewers, not just the pending ones.
Added an “Update from PR branch” action and fixed “Update from main/PR” silently refusing over untracked build output.
The Git section now reads sync, changes, and push state from the correct review worktree.
Review-agent files are seeded into every on-branch worktree so “Ready” always means the agent is really there.
